title: Token-level observability: add cost/latency breakdowns, improved tracing spans, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Production incidents over the past quarter showed that per-request aggregates hide token-level cost and latency patterns (eg: KV-cache misses, tokenization variance, and model tail latency). This PR adds token-level metrics, tracing spans, dashboards, and tuned alerts to make root-cause analysis and cost attribution more deterministic and reduce noisy alerts.

What this change does: - Adds a token-level metrics exporter that emits token_cost and token_latency metrics with labels: model, route, customer_tier, cache_hit (bool), and token_position_bucket. - Instruments tracing to emit per-token spans (lightweight) and propagate KV-cache context to link token events with cache hits/misses. - Introduces a new Token Cost & Latency dashboard (Grafana JSON) with templated panels and drilldowns from route -> model -> customer. - Adds alert tuning and new alert rules: SLO-based token-latency tail alerts, adaptive cooldowns, and sample-based anomaly alerts to reduce false positives from noisy microbursts. - Console: new Token dashboard route and component for customers with dedicated views and sampling controls. - Tests: unit and integration tests for aggregation, metric labels, and dashboard rendering.

Checklist: - [x] Metrics schema defined and backwards-compatible with existing aggregates - [x] Tracing instrumentation gated behind config flag (off by default for tiny clusters) - [x] Dashboard JSON and template generation script included - [x] Alert rules added with playbook entries and runbook links - [x] Integration tests exercising token aggregation and alert firing behavior

Backward compatibility and rollout: Metrics add new series but do not remove existing aggregates. Tracing instrumentation is behind a runtime flag controlled by configmap/helm value so rollout can be staged. Dashboard and alert changes are additive; alert thresholds default to conservative values and are part of a staged rollout (canary for 10% of routes).

How to test locally: 1) Start local dev runtime with METRICS_TOKEN_EXPORTER=true and SAMPLE_TRACING=true. 2) Run tests: go test ./runtimes/inference/metrics -run TokenMetrics 3) Use the provided scripts/examples to generate synthetic traffic with variable token distributions: scripts/generate-token-load.py 4) Load Grafana dashboard JSON into a local Grafana and validate panels and templated variables.

Notes: - We opted for a light-weight per-token span to avoid high cardinality in traces; spans are sampled and annotated with cache_hit and token_position_bucket to help identify costly tokens. - Alerts use a combination of SLO burn rate and sampled p99 token latency to reduce noise. See ENG-4876 for design doc details.
commits: Add token-level metrics exporter and aggregation logic (ENG-4876)
Expose token_cost and token_latency metrics with model/route/customer_tier labels
Instrument tracing spans per-token and add KV-cache context propagation
Add Token Cost & Latency Grafana dashboard and templated panels
Alert tuning: SLO-based thresholds, cooldown, and sample-based anomalies
Tests: unit + integration tests for metrics aggregation and dashboard templates
review_comments: Jonas Meyer: Can we ensure metric cardinality stays bounded? Suggest token_position_bucket instead of raw token index.
Aisha Patel: Implemented token_position_bucket (head/mid/tail) and added a note about sampling to docs.
Priya Desai: Alert thresholds look conservative. Will we tune them after canary? Also suggest adding cooldown to prevent flapping.
Aisha Patel: Added cooldown and cooldown window config; default conservative values and canary rollout notes included in playbook.
Liam O'Connor: Tracing spans look fine; ensure the default sample rate is low to avoid trace bill shock. Consider opt-in for small clusters.
Aisha Patel: Added feature flag and helm value SAMPLE_TRACING with documentation in metrics/README.md.

release_notes: Adds token-level cost and latency breakdown dashboards, lightweight per-token tracing spans (configurable), and tuned alerting to reduce false positives. Rollout is staged behind a config flag and conservative alert defaults.
